Echo asks Ruwen to help Ash, whose technically precise Bamboo Viper practice has stopped advancing. In Earth's responsive dungeon, Ruwen and Echo discover that Ash's seven awakened chakras have become a crutch that filters every movement. Sift reveals a deeper intuitive awareness than his usual behavior suggests, while Echo recognizes that her own rigid teaching has reinforced Ash's blockage. She changes course, using Blapy's extraordinary motorcycle to restore joy and direct experience to Ash's training. The visit also strengthens the theory that Earth guards a locked Outerverse bridge and that Ruwen's incomplete sword-key needs thirty-two golems. When Ruwen returns to recover battlefield loot, a countdown unexpectedly proves to be the delayed Inklord ceremony. He stores the combatants and treasure in his soul vault, but cannot alter his locked party. Ruwen and his companions are pulled into the event together as an Inklord conclave begins.

The Library of Alexandria isolates Ruwen inside a heavily suppressed contest where Inklords must gather bookmarks, solve the Archivist's riddle, and find the hidden exit. His Black Pyramid emblem makes him the most visible target. He aids Sarah, the Red Librarian, whose body-based magic and conscious red bracelet connect her to the Zealot and a world associated with the Mind and Body Towers. They form a temporary alliance, then summon Hamma, Sift, Rami, Echo, and Lylan. The group battles knowledge constructs while Rami absorbs their information. When her growing void-worm nature proves to have severed her old mental bond with Ruwen, he combines several magic systems to build a stable shared mental space. Rami can now transfer and organize the library's knowledge inside his expanding inner world. Although the immediate constructs are defeated, destroyed scouts show that another hostile force is approaching.

Tremine and Una join Ruwen's alliance during a fight with an Inkblot. The party then turns to a deceased rival Inklord whose memory of the library may solve the conclave. Hamma cannot resurrect the body because its soul, aura, and chakras are absent, but Echo uses her Death authority and the Grimoire of Mourning to raise it as an aware undead servant. The former rival remembers that Ruwen killed him and agrees to help in exchange for his journal and emblem. Echo appoints him the first Inklord of the Library of Final Passage. He explains that the conclave's rules are structured to push competitors into killing each other, and begins working through the Archivist's riddle. Meanwhile Archie warns that Ruwen and Sift's advanced soul power can manifest conceptual cards, a capacity that may attract dangerous Outerverse attention.

The undead Inklord and Tremine trace the Archivist riddle toward the Central Index, while Ruwen finds a separate alchemical reading that may describe the exit. The party defeats a Data Curator that copies their memories and techniques, with Tremine's chaos damaging it and Rami absorbing its indexed knowledge. Rami then uses Scarecrow-aspect clones as remote anchors to map the library. Una reveals that she wants to recover Isaac's champion, whose memories were suppressed. In the Overlooked Archive, Ruwen obtains a radiant meditation mat and completes its eight-gem activation. The process links chakra energy to his blood, suggesting a route to open blood nodes. The mat enters Ruwen's body, carries him underwater to an unknown place, and returns him to the shed through the intervention of a giant octopus. The destination and the lasting nature of the change remain unclear.

Ruwen learns that the meditation mat carried him into the Pool of Transcendence. The visit raised all eight chakras, improved their quality and potential dramatically, and granted new abilities tied to emotion, truth, dimensions, bonds, and magical balance. Rami has absorbed nearly the entire library and is identified as the perception worm, making both her and Ruwen targets for exceptional rewards. With healing and resurrection disabled, Ruwen approaches the surviving Inklords offering each one hundred books in exchange for safe passage. Many begin to accept, but Isaac's replacement Inklord intends betrayal and stands beside Isaac's champion. Hostile spatial interference turns Ruwen's movement into a deadly backlash against enemy mages. Then dimensional tears open around Isaac's force and release disguised servants of the Zealot, collapsing the negotiation into a new battle at the exit.

The disguised attackers are Zealot angels, and their reinforcements overwhelm the exit island. Ruwen becomes Valdor and learns to channel the seraph body's energy through the Destruction Realm, allowing him to survive the angels' detonations. Una is mortally poisoned while shielding Isaac's champion. Before dying, she restores his suppressed memories of their relationship. Ruwen rejects the failed resurrection systems and directly rebuilds Una's body, soul, aura, and chakras by combining blood, soul, mental, chakra, harmonic, and spirit magic. She revives. Ruwen closes the dimensional tears and defeats the remaining angels, while Rami repairs the void damage in her worm-like form. He permanently severs Isaac's champion from Isaac and lets the surviving Inklords escape. Sarah reveals that her bracelet is a conscious fragment of a Zealot-destroyed vessel and a key to a tower secret. Una and the freed champion depart for Grave. Ruwen postpones his prize, and he and Sift prepare to follow Sarah's portal toward the Mind and Body Towers.

characters.description: A spiteful, unwashed man who delights in cruel jokes, keeps caged monkeys, and catches birds for pies. Much of his attention is devoted to finding new ways to torment his wife and the animals around him.
characters.name: Mr Twit

characters.description: Mr Twit's equally malicious wife and frequent target of his tricks. She answers each humiliation with another trick of her own and shares his cruelty toward animals.
characters.name: Mrs Twit

characters.description: The father of a family of monkeys imprisoned in the Twits' garden. Forced to perform upside down for a circus act the Twits hope to create, he waits for a way to free his family.
characters.name: Muggle-Wump

characters.description: A traveling bird who can understand Muggle-Wump and communicate with the local birds. His shared language with the captive monkeys makes him a valuable friend outside the Twits' garden.
characters.name: The Roly-Poly Bird

characters.description: A young boy who ignores his mother's warning and enters the dangerous Forest of Sin. Pursued by a fire-breathing creature, he finds refuge among the tiny people living high in the trees.
characters.name: Little Billy

characters.description: The leader of the Minpins, a secret community of miniature people who live inside hollow trees. He welcomes Billy but explains that the monster below prevents the Minpins from walking safely on the ground.
characters.name: Don Mini

characters.description: A large, fire-breathing beast that hunts in the Forest of Sin. It drives Billy up a tree and terrorizes the Minpins by patrolling the ground beneath their homes.
characters.name: The Gruncher

characters.description: A great bird trusted by the Minpins as a safe means of traveling above the forest. It is strong enough to carry Billy between their treetop homes without exposing him to the ground below.
characters.name: The Swan

characters.description: An eight-year-old girl who narrates her encounter with the Gregg family. When anger overwhelms her, a strange power in her pointing finger can transform the people who have provoked her.
characters.name: The Girl

characters.description: The Girl's neighbor, an enthusiastic hunter who takes his sons shooting despite her objections. He dismisses her anger and proudly brings home the birds they have killed.
characters.name: Mr Gregg

characters.description: Mr Gregg's wife and the mother of William and Philip. She is caught in the same transformation as the hunters and must help her family survive when their home is occupied by armed ducks.
characters.name: Mrs Gregg

characters.description: One of the Gregg sons, who joins his father on a duck hunt. He later has to experience the vulnerability of a bird rather than the security of the person holding the gun.
characters.name: William Gregg

characters.description: William's brother and another participant in the Gregg family's hunting. The magic affecting the household leaves him with wings and forces him to reconsider the sport.
characters.name: Philip Gregg

recaps.ending: In the final story, the Gregg family awaken with wings and are displaced by four large ducks with human arms. Forced to live in a nest and threatened with the guns they once used for sport, the Greggs promise never to hunt again. The ducks accept the promise, and the family eventually regain their ordinary bodies. Mr Gregg destroys the guns and changes the household's behavior toward birds. The Girl then learns that her magical finger has found a new target: another local family associated with hunting now appear to have taken on chicken-like traits. The collection therefore closes with the Greggs reformed but the mysterious power still active. Earlier, the Twits vanished after the escaped animals inverted their house, and Little Billy saved the Minpins from the Gruncher while preserving their existence as a secret.
recaps.in_short: Three stories reverse the power held by bullies, monsters, and hunters. In The Twits, the captive Muggle-Wump family and their bird allies escape, glue the Twits' furniture to the ceiling, and convince the returning couple that they are upside down; the Twits stand on their heads until they shrink away. In The Minpins, Little Billy disobeys his mother and enters a forbidden forest, where tiny tree-dwellers shelter him from the fire-breathing Gruncher. Riding a Swan, Billy lures the beast into a lake and frees the Minpins from its rule. In The Magic Finger, a girl's anger transforms the duck-hunting Gregg family into winged, tiny people while ducks occupy their house and wield their guns. After experiencing life as prey, the Greggs swear off hunting, return to normal, and destroy their weapons, while the Girl's unexplained magic moves on to another offending household.

recaps.text: Mr and Mrs Twit are a cruel couple who spend much of their time playing escalating tricks on each other. Their private warfare includes disgusting food, concealed creatures, and a scheme that makes Mrs Twit believe she is steadily shrinking. Their cruelty extends beyond the marriage: they imprison Muggle-Wump and his family of monkeys, forcing them to practice standing upside down, and spread strong glue on a tree so that visiting birds can be baked in a pie. The Roly-Poly Bird helps the monkeys warn the birds away. While the Twits are absent, the animals escape and attach the household furniture to the ceiling. On returning, the couple believe the whole room has turned upside down and stand on their heads to correct themselves. Glue fixes them there, and they shrink until nothing remains. The animals are free to return home.

After the Twits are defeated by their captives, Little Billy enters the Forest of Sin despite his mother's warnings. The fire-breathing Gruncher chases him up a tree, where he discovers the Minpins, tiny people whose connected homes occupy the hollow trunks. Their leader, Don Mini, explains that birds provide transportation but that the monster makes the forest floor deadly. Billy learns to ride a Swan and devises a way to help. He draws the Gruncher into a pursuit, stays just ahead of it, and flies out over a lake. When the Swan rises beyond reach, the charging beast plunges into the water and is destroyed. The Minpins can safely use the ground again. Billy returns home and keeps their community secret, but the Swan continues to collect him for nighttime flights and visits with his new friends.

The final narrator is a girl whose finger produces transformative magic whenever her anger becomes intense. She objects to the Gregg family's enthusiasm for shooting animals, especially after Mr Gregg and his sons kill ducks. Her anger triggers the power. The next morning, Mr and Mrs Gregg and their sons are tiny and winged, while four human-sized ducks occupy their house with human arms and the family's guns. The Greggs build a nest in a tree and confront hunger, cold, and the fear of being shot. When the ducks threaten them, the family promise to abandon hunting. They regain their normal forms, destroy the guns, and begin treating birds differently. The Girl then discovers signs that the power has affected another hunting family, showing that the Magic Finger remains beyond her control and that the Greggs' lesson is not its final intervention.

characters.description: A dark elf ranger reunited with the friends he mistakenly mourned, though the war has taken Tarathiel and Delly and left Bruenor badly wounded. Drizzt now fights with allies again while trying to distinguish defense from the vengeance that nearly consumed him.
characters.name: Drizzt Do'Urden

characters.description: King of Mithral Hall, gravely injured in the defense that stopped Obould's immediate assault. Bruenor's survival matters to the dwarves as both a personal hope and a political question, since a continuing war requires someone able to unite scattered forces.
characters.name: Bruenor Battlehammer

characters.description: Bruenor's adopted daughter and Drizzt's partner. Catti-brie helps hold the companions together around Bruenor's sickbed and brings Taulmaril to the renewed fighting when the siege gives way to a struggle over the surrounding land.
characters.name: Catti-brie

characters.description: Bruenor's foster son, carrying Aegis-fang and grieving Delly's death. Wulfgar must decide what responsibility to Colson now requires and whether his future lies with the companions or with the northern people from whom he first came.
characters.name: Wulfgar

characters.description: The halfling member of the Companions of the Hall. Regis survives the siege and supports Wulfgar through the practical journey created by Delly's death, while remaining a trusted scout and negotiator in Bruenor's wider cause.
characters.name: Regis

characters.description: The child whom Wulfgar and Delly raised after leaving Auckney. With Delly dead and war surrounding Mithral Hall, Colson's need for a secure home forces Wulfgar to settle an obligation that courage in battle cannot answer.
characters.name: Colson

characters.description: The elf warrior who helped pull Drizzt out of solitary vengeance. Innovindil continues the campaign after Obould killed Tarathiel, combining aerial scouting and patience with a determination that grief should sharpen her purpose without owning it.
characters.name: Innovindil

characters.description: The orc king whose army has failed to take Mithral Hall but controls much of the country around it. Obould must turn a coalition built for conquest into something that can survive winter, rival chiefs and the competing ambitions of his giant allies.
characters.name: Obould Many-Arrows

characters.description: The frost giant leader allied with Obould. Gerti's warriors remain the coalition's strongest answer to dwarven fortifications, but she has her own claim to authority and no intention of letting an orc king convert her aid into permanent command over the giants.
characters.name: Gerti Orelsdottr

characters.description: A veteran commander responsible for Mithral Hall's disciplined defense. Banak must convert survival under siege into a workable campaign outside the gates without spending dwarf lives as if Obould's enormous host can be defeated in one charge.
characters.name: Banak Brawnanvil

characters.description: The shield dwarf leader whose break with Mirabar brought experienced soldiers to Bruenor's side. Torgar helps connect Mithral Hall's defense to the wider dwarf response and presses for action against the invaders holding the surface approaches.
characters.name: Torgar Hammerstriker

characters.description: Mirabar's sceptrana and an ally of the dwarves after choosing regional defense over her city's cautious politics. Shoudra's magic and judgment remain useful as Bruenor's coalition shifts from holding fixed fortifications to coordinating separate forces.
characters.name: Shoudra Stargleam

characters.description: The gnome inventor whose explosives helped save Mithral Hall. Nanfoodle remains with the defenders as they assess what his devices accomplished and look for ways to contest an enemy who still holds the numerical advantage.
characters.name: Nanfoodle Buswilligan

characters.description: A drow swordsman embedded in the forces that helped unleash Obould's invasion. Tos'un has survived the collapse of the hidden drow scheme and now looks for an escape from allies who are increasingly willing to spend one another for advantage.
characters.name: Tos'un Armgo

recaps.ending: Bruenor recovers enough to resume command and the dwarves carry the war back outside Mithral Hall, coordinating with allied forces to break Obould's immediate hold on the approaches. The renewed fighting ends the frost giants' decisive support for the invasion. The defenders win important battles but cannot destroy the enormous orc population or remove Obould, whose strength and authority survive every attempt to reduce the war to a duel. Obould, in turn, cannot conquer Mithral Hall and begins acting as the ruler of occupied territory rather than the leader of an endlessly advancing horde. That balance leaves the North divided and opens the possibility of a settlement without making either side trust the other. Wulfgar and Regis return Colson to Meralda in Auckney, ending the improvised parenthood that Delly helped sustain; Wulfgar then turns back toward his own northern people. Drizzt and Catti-brie remain together, and Innovindil's companionship has helped Drizzt accept that a long life requires releasing the dead without abandoning them. The companions survive, but Obould's realm remains a fact the dwarves must confront rather than a raiding force they can simply chase away.
recaps.in_short: Mithral Hall has survived Obould's siege, but Bruenor is gravely wounded, Delly and Tarathiel are dead and the orc host controls much of the surrounding land. As Bruenor recovers, Banak, Torgar, Shoudra and Nanfoodle help turn a desperate defense into a coordinated dwarf counteroffensive. Drizzt and Innovindil fight with purpose rather than blind revenge, while Obould struggles to hold together orcs, giants and hidden drow whose interests are separating. Wulfgar and Regis take Colson back to Auckney and return the child to Meralda, allowing Wulfgar to face Delly's loss and choose his own people again. The renewed campaign breaks the giants' support, but Obould survives and the dwarves cannot remove the vast orc population from the territory it occupies. Mithral Hall remains free, Obould begins governing a durable realm and the war settles into a balance that force alone cannot resolve. Drizzt and Catti-brie remain together as the immediate crisis ends.

recaps.text: Previously: King Obould Many-Arrows united orc tribes, allied with Gerti Orelsdottr's frost giants and invaded the northern lands around Mithral Hall. Hidden drow agents encouraged the war while Mirabar's divided response drove Sceptrana Shoudra Stargleam, Torgar Hammerstriker and Nanfoodle Buswilligan into Bruenor's coalition. At Shallows, Drizzt saw a tower collapse and wrongly concluded that Bruenor, Catti-brie and Regis had died, though all three escaped. His grief drove a solitary campaign until the elves Innovindil and Tarathiel joined him. Obould killed Tarathiel and survived Drizzt's challenge. At Mithral Hall, Nanfoodle's explosives broke a giant-supported assault, but Bruenor was gravely wounded and Delly Curtie was killed, leaving Colson in the companions' care. Drizzt finally reached the hall and learned his friends were alive. The companions begin this book reunited but diminished, with Obould undefeated and a great orc population holding the land outside the dwarves' surviving fortress.

Mithral Hall has survived the attack without ending the siege. Bruenor lies gravely wounded, and the uncertainty around his recovery weighs on a clan that depends on him for more than battlefield orders. Catti-brie, Drizzt, Wulfgar and Regis remain close while Banak Brawnanvil maintains the defenses and Torgar, Shoudra and Nanfoodle assess what forces can still be used outside the gates. Wulfgar grieves Delly while caring for Colson, a responsibility that now requires a decision about the child's permanent home. Drizzt is no longer fighting under the false belief that his companions are dead, but Tarathiel's murder and Obould's survival leave vengeance close at hand. Innovindil continues beside him, insisting through her conduct that mourning need not become surrender. Across the occupied land, Obould faces a different problem: his horde won territory, but feeding, disciplining and governing its many tribes will determine whether the conquest lasts.

Obould works to turn military momentum into a durable realm, balancing chiefs who expect plunder, shamans who proclaim divine purpose, frost giants who consider themselves partners and drow survivors who never intended an orc kingdom to become independent. His forces continue attacking exposed communities so that Mithral Hall cannot gather relief without risking the people beyond its walls. Drizzt and Innovindil scout and strike with narrower tactical goals than Drizzt's earlier solitary rampage. They learn that Obould's army is becoming harder to treat as one target: some bands obey a king's strategy while others follow local ambition. Inside the hall, Banak preserves strength for the right opening instead of answering every provocation. Bruenor's condition begins to improve, allowing hope of a coordinated response. Wulfgar accepts that keeping Colson near a battlefield because he fears another separation would repeat the possessiveness and avoidance that once governed his own recovery.

Bruenor recovers sufficiently to take part in planning and refuses to let survival inside Mithral Hall count as victory while allies and settlements remain exposed. His return restores direction to the dwarf coalition, though Banak and the others temper his desire for an immediate decisive blow. Torgar helps connect forces displaced by Mirabar's earlier caution, while Shoudra and Nanfoodle support a campaign that must rely on timing and position rather than equal numbers. The companions' roads divide according to need. Drizzt and Catti-brie remain central to the military effort, and Innovindil keeps watch on Obould's movements and the giant alliance. Wulfgar and Regis take responsibility for moving Colson away from the war and toward Auckney, where the truth of the child's birth and Meralda's claim can finally be addressed. The choice is painful precisely because Wulfgar has become a genuine father to the child, not because he has failed at the role.

The dwarves begin a broader counteroffensive, combining Mithral Hall's veterans with allied companies and using strong ground to keep Obould from bringing the full host against one point. Bruenor's recovery gives the campaign a visible leader, while Banak and Torgar supply the discipline needed to prevent enthusiasm from turning into an exposed charge. Drizzt and Catti-brie attack the enemy's mobility and command rather than counting ordinary soldiers slain, a change from the ranger's vengeance after Shallows. Innovindil continues to pursue justice for Tarathiel without mistaking her own death for payment. Obould gives ground where necessary and preserves the core of his army, behaving more like a king protecting future power than a raider demanding constant advance. Friction grows with Gerti's giants and with the remaining drow agents, whose expectation that the orcs would exhaust themselves has not been met. Neither coalition is as unified as it appears from the opposing line.

Winter slows the largest movements and exposes the political shape beneath the fighting. Obould must keep tribes fed and loyal while defending land already taken; permanent camps, patrols and rules begin replacing the horde's first rush. The dwarves use the pause to regroup and coordinate attacks against the alliance's strongest separate elements. Gerti's frost giants remain formidable, but their partnership with Obould is strained by competing pride and by the orc king's refusal to remain dependent on them. The hidden drow cause fractures of their own as personal survival overtakes the original plan. Away from the main armies, Wulfgar and Regis complete the difficult journey created by Delly's death. They bring Colson back to Meralda in Auckney, giving the child a safe home connected to her birth rather than keeping her inside Wulfgar's war. The farewell leaves Wulfgar grieving both Delly and the family life they briefly made, but free to choose his next allegiance honestly.

Bruenor's coalition launches its strongest renewed effort and wins back control of critical approaches to Mithral Hall. The fighting breaks the frost giants' decisive support and removes the siege power on which Obould's early victories depended. Dwarf and allied forces inflict serious losses, but Obould preserves enough of his army to prevent the campaign from becoming a complete expulsion. He remains personally dangerous and politically established; the occupied orcs are now too numerous and rooted to be erased by one victory. Mithral Hall is secure, yet the region is divided between powers neither able to conquer the other without ruin. Obould begins governing what he holds, creating the basis for a settlement even while Bruenor and the companions distrust him. Wulfgar and Regis return after placing Colson with Meralda, and Wulfgar turns toward the northern people and identity he had long avoided. Innovindil has helped Drizzt understand that honoring Tarathiel and the other dead does not require living only for revenge. Drizzt and Catti-brie remain together as the Companions of the Hall move out of the immediate crisis into an uneasy new political world.

characters.description: Heir of ancient kings and now a leader of the broken Fellowship, who takes command after tragedy and pursues the enemy across the plains of Rohan. Steadfast and enduring, he moves ever closer to accepting the destiny he has long kept hidden.
characters.name: Aragorn

characters.description: An elf of the northern woods, keen-eyed and swift with a bow, one of the Fellowship who stays at Aragorn's side. His unlikely, deepening friendship with the dwarf Gimli grows as they run and fight together through the wars of Rohan.
characters.name: Legolas

characters.description: A stout, doughty dwarf of the Fellowship, proud and quick to anger but stout-hearted, who keeps pace with Aragorn and Legolas on the long chase and stands with them through the battles that follow.
characters.name: Gimli

characters.description: The wizard, thought lost in the mines of Moria, who returns transformed and robed in white with his power renewed for the struggle ahead. He rejoins Aragorn's company and sets about freeing Rohan from the enemy's grip.
characters.name: Gandalf the White

characters.description: The oldest of the Ents, the tree-like shepherds of the forest, slow to speak and slower to anger. He takes in two lost hobbits and, once finally roused, gathers his kind to march against the wizard who has been felling his trees.
characters.name: Treebeard

characters.description: The aging king of Rohan, long weighed down and misled by a treacherous whispering counselor, until Gandalf frees him from his despair. Renewed in spirit, he takes up his sword and rides to defend his people in war.
characters.name: Théoden

characters.description: A great wizard, once the head of his order, who has turned to seeking power for himself and breeds an army in his fortress of Isengard. He covets the ring and makes war on Rohan, and his persuasive voice can sway the minds of those who stop to listen.
characters.name: Saruman

characters.description: Bearer of the One Ring, pressing on toward Mordor with Sam after the Fellowship's breaking. The ring grows heavier on him with every mile, and he must decide whether to trust a treacherous guide who claims to know the secret ways into the enemy's land.
characters.name: Frodo Baggins

characters.description: Frodo's loyal companion, sturdy and stubbornly faithful, who watches over his master's dwindling strength and distrusts every promise of the wretched creature that offers to lead them onward.
characters.name: Samwise Gamgee

characters.description: The wretched creature who once owned the ring and still hungers for it, captured by Frodo and Sam and bound to serve as their guide. Torn between a cringing wish to please his new master and his consuming craving for the precious, he leads them toward a secret pass.
characters.name: Gollum

recaps.ending: The Two Towers ends with its two strands left on the edge of crisis. In the west, the immediate threats have been beaten: Saruman is broken and shut in his tower at Isengard, his army destroyed at Helm's Deep, and Rohan is roused and allied with Gandalf. But the far greater power of Sauron has not yet been faced, and after Pippin's rash look into the enemy's seeing-stone drew the Dark Lord's eye, Gandalf has ridden with the hobbit to the threatened city of Minas Tirith, expecting Mordor's assault to fall on Gondor next. Aragorn, Theoden, and the others are left to gather their strength for the war to come. In the east, the situation is dire. Frodo has been stung by the great spider Shelob and carried off, paralysed, into the orc-tower of Cirith Ungol. Sam, who briefly took up the ring believing his master dead, has learned from the orcs' own talk that Frodo lives and is only poisoned, but he is now alone, poorly armed against a garrison, and shut outside the tower gate with the ring still to be destroyed. Both quests hang unresolved: the war for Gondor about to begin, and the ring-bearer a captive deep in enemy land.
recaps.in_short: With the Fellowship broken, the story follows two paths. Boromir dies defending the hobbits Merry and Pippin, who are captured by orcs; Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli pursue them into Rohan. The hobbits escape into Fangorn Forest and rouse the tree-giant Ents against the wizard Saruman. The hunters meet Gandalf, returned from death as Gandalf the White, and together they free King Theoden of Rohan from Saruman's influence and win the battle of Helm's Deep, while the Ents destroy Saruman's fortress of Isengard and trap him in his tower. Pippin looks into a captured seeing-stone and is glimpsed by Sauron, and Gandalf carries him off toward Gondor. Meanwhile Frodo and Sam, guided by the treacherous creature Gollum, cross the Dead Marshes toward Mordor. Barred at the Black Gate, they take a secret southern path, are briefly held and then released by Boromir's honorable brother Faramir, and climb toward a hidden pass. There Gollum betrays them to the giant spider Shelob, who poisons Frodo. Sam, thinking his master dead, takes the ring, then learns Frodo is alive but captured by orcs, and the book ends with Frodo imprisoned and Sam outside alone.

recaps.text: The One Ring of the Dark Lord Sauron came into the keeping of the hobbit Frodo Baggins, and a Fellowship of nine set out to carry it into Sauron's land of Mordor and destroy it in the fire where it was forged. Their road was hard. In the mines of Moria the wizard Gandalf fell into a chasm fighting a demon of fire, the Balrog, and was lost. The survivors were sheltered by the elf-lady Galadriel and travelled on by river. At the last the man Boromir, a lord of Gondor, was overcome by longing for the ring and tried to take it from Frodo. Fearing what the ring could do even to good men, Frodo resolved to go on to Mordor alone, and only his servant Sam managed to follow him; the two crossed the river together. The rest of the company was scattered along the shore, Gandalf believed dead, and the quest split in two: two hobbits creeping toward the Enemy's country, and the broken Fellowship left behind as war gathers over Middle-earth.

At the river's edge the Fellowship's break turns to disaster. A band of orcs attacks; Boromir, repenting his attempt on the ring, dies fighting to defend the hobbits Merry and Pippin, but the two are seized and carried off, while Frodo and Sam are already gone toward Mordor. Aragorn finds the dying Boromir, and with Legolas and Gimli lays him in a boat sent over the falls, then the three set out on foot to rescue the captured hobbits, running for days across the grasslands of Rohan on the orcs' trail. They meet Eomer, a young marshal of Rohan, who has just destroyed a company of orcs near the eaves of a forest and lends them horses, though his king has forbidden dealings with strangers. Meanwhile Merry and Pippin, dragged along as prisoners, seize a moment of confusion during the Rohirrim's night attack to cut their bonds and slip away into the dark trees of Fangorn Forest.

In the ancient forest of Fangorn, Merry and Pippin meet Treebeard, the eldest of the Ents, great tree-herds who look after the woods. Alarmed by news of Saruman's axes and burnings on his borders, Treebeard summons the other Ents to a slow council to decide whether to go to war. On the plains outside, Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli follow the hobbits' trail into the forest and are astonished to meet an old man robed in white: Gandalf, returned from death. He tells them that he fought the Balrog to its end, passed through death, and has been sent back with greater power for the task still ahead, now Gandalf the White. He turns their thoughts from the lost hobbits, whom he says are safe among the Ents, toward the immediate danger of Saruman and the threatened kingdom of Rohan. Reunited with his old horse Shadowfax, Gandalf leads Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli out of the forest to ride for the halls of the Rohan king, whom Saruman's malice has left weak and ill-counselled.

Gandalf leads the three companions to Edoras, hall of King Theoden of Rohan, whom he finds aged and despairing under the poisonous counsel of the servant Wormtongue, an agent of Saruman. Gandalf breaks the spell over him; Theoden casts out Wormtongue, takes up his sword, and rouses his people to war. As Saruman's great army marches on Rohan, Theoden and his men make their stand at the mountain fortress of Helm's Deep. Through a night of desperate assault the wall is breached, but they hold, and at dawn Gandalf returns with fresh riders and the enemy is broken. Meanwhile the Ents, having decided at last to act, storm Saruman's stronghold of Isengard, smash its works, and flood the valley, trapping the wizard in his tower of Orthanc. Riding to Isengard, Gandalf's company is met at the ruined gates by Merry and Pippin, safe and reunited with their friends.

At the wreck of Isengard the hobbits tell their tale, and the company parleys with the imprisoned Saruman. His voice is seductive and nearly wins some of the listeners over, but Gandalf resists him, and when Saruman refuses to repent, Gandalf breaks his staff and casts him out of the order of wizards. Wormtongue, in spite or clumsiness, hurls down a heavy dark globe from the tower, and Pippin retrieves it. That night, unable to master his curiosity, Pippin looks into the globe, a palantir or seeing-stone, and is caught in a vision by Sauron himself, who believes the hobbit is the ring-bearer held captive by Saruman. Shaken but unharmed, Pippin is questioned by Gandalf, who grasps the stone's danger. As a winged enemy scout passes overhead, Gandalf takes Pippin up and rides hard for Minas Tirith in Gondor, to warn the city and to keep the reckless hobbit close.

The book turns to Frodo and Sam, lost in the barren, broken hills on the edge of Mordor. Gollum, the ring's former owner, has been trailing them, and they capture him; Frodo spares his life and binds him with a promise to guide them, while Sam remains deeply suspicious. Gollum, torn between his old craving for the ring and a grudging loyalty to Frodo, leads them across the Dead Marshes, a haunted bog where the faces of ancient dead seem to float beneath the water. They come to the Black Gate, the northern entrance to Mordor, and find it shut fast and heavily guarded, impossible to pass; on the way they watch fierce men from the south marching to join Sauron's muster. Gollum tells them of another way in, a secret path far to the south, and, having no better choice, Frodo agrees to trust him and turn aside toward it.

Following Gollum south through the green land of Ithilien, the hobbits are captured by a company of Gondor's rangers led by Faramir, the brother of Boromir. Faramir questions them and learns of Boromir's death and, by a slip of Sam's, of the ring they carry. Unlike his brother, he masters the temptation and swears he would not take the thing even if he found it lying in the road. He shelters them at a hidden refuge behind a waterfall. There Gollum is caught fishing in a forbidden pool below, and Faramir, understanding that Frodo needs the creature as a guide, spares his life at Frodo's plea rather than have his men shoot him. Warning them that the path Gollum means to take is evil and rumored to be guarded by a nameless terror, Faramir nonetheless lets the three go on, giving them supplies and his blessing.

Gollum guides the hobbits past the old cross-roads and up toward the high pass of Cirith Ungol, climbing a long series of steep stairs while secretly plotting to betray them. He briefly wavers toward pity, but Sam's mistrustful words harden him. Leading them into a black tunnel through the mountains, Gollum abandons them to Shelob, a monstrous ancient spider that lairs there. Shelob stings Frodo, who falls cold and paralysed; Sam, believing his master dead, fights the spider off with Frodo's sword and the phial of light from Galadriel, driving her back wounded. Torn by grief and duty, Sam takes the ring and the quest upon himself. But orcs come down from the tower above and carry Frodo's body away, and Sam, following invisibly, overhears them say that Frodo is not dead at all but only poisoned and will wake. The book ends with Sam alone and desperate outside the shut gate of the enemy's tower, his master a prisoner within.
